facts.text: home() sends G28, move_to() sends G1 X... Y... Z... F... with three decimals, and wait_for_moves() sends M400
send() writes the command with a trailing newline and waits for a reply line equal to 'ok' or starting with 'ok '
send() and query() default max_secs to 30.0
send_and_wait_for_ok raises TimeoutError when no ok arrives before max_secs
GantryConfig defaults the feedrate to 3000 mm/min
M114 reports the current XYZE position as Marlin sees it
The documented M114 reply is X:0.000 Y:0.000 Z:0.000 E:0.000 followed by ok
M112 is the emergency stop: Marlin halts and refuses commands until power-cycle
G28 homes all axes (X, then Y, then Z)
After head removal G28 succeeds for X and Y but can hang or crash on Z; the clone says to use G28 X Y until a Z-endstop strategy exists
G28 X Y is the XY homing command of the safe_home path
Soft limits are not enforced in software and any hardcoded coordinate is untrusted
The print head, hotend, fan, sensor PCB and heater wiring have been physically removed from the carriage
The i3 Mega is no longer a 3D printer; it is a 3-axis motion platform
The dPette is a separate USB device whose 6-byte serial protocol is delegated to the external dpette-usb-driver package
PipetteBot.aspirate_at moves, waits for the moves (M400), then calls the pipette's aspirate
The gantry serial link is 250000 8N1 on stock Anycubic firmware
